title: Mechanistic Interpretability Needs a Logic of Inference
abstract: arXiv:2611.14483v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Neural networks are increasingly studied not merely as predictive systems, but as complex systems whose internal computations are themselves objects of scientific inquiry. Recent progress in mechanistic interpretability (MI) has made it possible to identify neurons, features, circuits, population structures, and dynamical patterns associated with model behavior. As these tools improve, attention is shifting from what can be observed inside a model to how those observations support mechanistic explanations. We examine the parallel efforts of neuroscience and MI to address this question and identify recurring inferential bottlenecks when inferring mechanisms from complex neural systems. We propose five principles and organize them into a recursive logic for a more rigorous procedure of mechanistic inference. These principles provide a framework that supports scientific discovery in two senses: it helps turn local interpretability findings

translated_title: 机制可解释性需要一种推理逻辑
translated_abstract: 神经网络越来越多地不仅被当作预测系统来研究，而且被当作其内部计算本身就是科学研究对象的复杂系统来研究。机制可解释性（MI）领域的最新进展使得识别与模型行为相关的神经元、特征、回路、群体结构和动态模式成为可能。随着这些工具的不断改进，研究注意力正从“模型内部能观察到什么”转向“这些观察如何支持机制性解释”。我们考察了神经科学与机制可解释性在解决这一问题上的并行努力，并识别出从复杂神经系统中推断机制时反复出现的推理瓶颈。我们提出五项原则，并将其组织成一个递归逻辑，从而形成更严谨的机制推断程序。这些原则提供了一个框架，在两个层面上支持科学发现：它有助于将局部的可解释性发现……
tldr: 该论文指出现有机制可解释性研究需要一套严谨的推理逻辑，提出由五项原则构成的递归逻辑框架，以解决从复杂神经系统中推断机制时反复出现的推理瓶颈问题。
en_tdlr: This paper argues that mechanistic interpretability requires a rigorous logic of inference, proposing five principles organized into a recursive logic framework to address recurring inferential bottlenecks when inferring mechanisms from complex neural systems.
